close_reason: Fixed in commit fce9ae9. Added defense-in-depth account_exists check at the top of MemoryBackend.create_object — returns BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError("unknown account: ...")). Removed the redundant known_accounts.insert at the success path. Added unit test create_object_unknown_account_errors_without_registering. Discovered the same silent-auto-register pattern in the objects_mut helper (workspace-wide cookie-cut across mail/chat/calendars/tasks/contacts/sharing/metadata servers); filed as JMAP-ayoz.36 for canonical-first propagation. All 31 tests pass; clippy --all-features clean.
description:
memory.rs:637 — MemoryBackend::create_object unconditionally executes:

    inner.known_accounts.insert(account_id.as_ref().to_owned());

…on the success path BEFORE any account-existence check. This means a /set call carrying an arbitrary accountId string will silently bring that account into existence in the backend's known_accounts set, after which account_exists() returns true for it.

Trigger: any client call that reaches create_object with an account_id the backend did not previously know about. With JMAP-ayoz.1 (missing account_exists guard in handle_metadata_set) this is reachable from the wire. Even with that guard fixed, the auto-registration is wrong in principle: create_object is a per-object mutation, not an account lifecycle operation.

Actual behavior: backend silently extends its known account set during /set. A subsequent account_exists() for the same id returns true even though no account was ever registered via new_with_accounts or any explicit account-creation API.

Expected: create_object MUST return BackendSetError::SetError(SetError::new(SetErrorType::Forbidden)) or BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError("unknown account")) for an unknown account_id. The MetadataBackend trait doc does not promise auto-account-creation, so backends should not silently grow account state on a per-object call.

Fix: remove the  line at memory.rs:637 and gate create_object on account presence. Add an integration test asserting create_object with an unknown account_id returns an error and does NOT add the account to known_accounts.

Severity reasons:
1. Operational: a real backend with the same shape would attach private metadata records to phantom accounts.
2. Demo-impl precedent: contributors copy this shape into real backends.
3. Combined with JMAP-ayoz.1, this is exploitable from the wire as a defense-in-depth gap.
title: MemoryBackend.create_object silently registers unknown accounts via known_accounts.insert
